name: Modal spells: each mode's picker reads its own line, and picked modes survive a new X
notes: Found by the audit's per-mode check (tests/audit.js auditModes). Origin of Metalbending's "Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature you control. It gains indestructible" listed your artifacts and enchantments: the grant's subject "It" was placed where its match began, the end of the line before, so _pronounAntecedentRestriction took the words of the other mode's target ("artifact or enchantment"); a spell's pronoun subject reached across a "." is now placed at its own sentence (haveAbilityRegex and boostRegex), as a subject naming its own target already was. Invigorated Rampage's "Target creature gets +4/+0" had a picker of two: maxTargets was propagated across every effect of the spell, the other mode's "Two target creatures" included; for a modal spell it is propagated mode by mode, and getEffectInfo / the multi-target picker no longer read switched-off effects (another mode's count, restriction or opponent / you-control rule). Profane Command went back to its first modes when X was typed after picking modes (setXValue and _reparseWithChoices re-parse; _carryModalModes keeps the picks), and with "-X/-X" and "Up to X target creatures gain fear" picked together the fear mode had one picker for X targets: a mode of up to N now has N pickers in the per-mode list (setModalModeTarget's slotIndex, saved as modalTargetIds). Ent's Fury's "Then that creature gets +1/+1" now takes its target's words less the "if its power is 4 or greater" condition.
